terms.comment: Talk of all sorts is varius sermō. For various reasons is multīs dē causīs (Caes. BG 4.16; Traupman 106, 369).

terms.gloss: different, of different kinds; going different ways
terms.comment: Stronger than varius: things set apart from one another (see different).

terms.grammar: adjective, third declension, plural only; neuter also complūria (mostly early Latin)
terms.comment: For “various” meaning “several”, with no stress on their being different.

phrases.latin: convīviumque vīcīnōrum cotīdiē compleō, quod ad multam noctem quam maximē possumus variō sermōne prōdūcimus
phrases.english: every day I fill my table with neighbours, and we draw the evening out as far into the night as we can with talk of every kind

phrases.latin: ita variīs sermōnibus vespera extenditur, et quamquam longissimus diēs bene conditur
phrases.english: so the evening is drawn out with talk of various kinds, and even the longest day is well laid to rest

sources: Lewis & Short: varius · Lewis & Short: diversus · Lewis & Short: complures
